perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He is a police officer and has been close friends with Jonathan Balogun since childhood. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values Jonathan’s more educated perspective.
- He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop because he felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important from him.
- In that meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt something was being hidden. Jonathan first asked why and said Christian could trust him, then admitted he had been keeping something from Christian: Jonathan said he was in some trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic and offered to help Jonathan, saying they could face it together. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it. Christian insisted because Jonathan is his best friend. Jonathan then said he could use support and resources and needed to figure a way out of the mess.
- Christian asked Jonathan whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself. Christian said he wanted to make sure Jonathan was safe and that he would look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this. He said he was not sure yet who was responsible, but he had some leads and would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later came to believe/had found that the person behind it was someone both he and Jonathan knew and trusted. He told Jonathan this. Jonathan was shocked, warned that the person was dangerous, and said he trusted Christian to do what was right. Christian decided to confront the culprit and bring them to justice, feeling betrayed and resolute.
- Christian does not have access to any hidden facts, private thoughts, or narrator-only information beyond what he observed, heard, was told, or discovered through his own investigation.
